findings.title: Provider timeouts are classified as cancellation
findings.evidence: The loop over value.error, details.error, value.reason and details.reason returns true for the bare strings "cancelled" and "timeout". The function's own doc comment says the check must stay deliberately exact so that arbitrary provider errors are not promoted to cancellation. A provider-reported timeout therefore becomes indistinguishable from a user stop.
evidenceQuotes: if (candidate === "aborted" || candidate === "AbortError" || candidate === "ABORT_ERR" || candidate === "cancelled" || candidate === "timeout") return true;

reviewerEvidenceQuotes: if (candidate === "aborted" || candidate === "AbortError" || candidate === "ABORT_ERR" || candidate === "cancelled" || candidate === "timeout") return true;
Keep this check deliberately exact: arbitrary provider errors must not be
findings.rationale: Commit 654f639 ('treat cancelled/timeout as cancellation') widened the classifier, which contradicts the comment directly above it. Any caller that uses this predicate to decide between user-cancelled and failed will report a provider timeout as a user cancellation. That can suppress retry or failure diagnostics and misstate the run outcome. Timeout is an error condition, not a user-initiated stop, so the two should not share one classification. No in-repo caller of isWorkflowReturnedCancellation exists under src/, so the impact rests on external consumers of this exported function, which the contract treats as part of the API.
findings.recommendedAction: Remove "timeout" (and probably "cancelled" for error/reason fields) from the bare-string allowlist, or return a distinct timeout classification. Keep cancellation limited to explicit AbortError, cancelled:true, or an explicit cancellation marker. Add a regression test where {error:"timeout"} is not classified as cancellation.

findings.title: Stop-request detection matches on error message text
findings.evidence: isWorkflowStopRequestedError returns true when error.name equals WorkflowStopRequested or when error.message starts with the prefix "workflow stop requested". Classification therefore depends on free-form text, not on a typed marker.
findings.rationale: Any Error whose message begins with that phrase is treated as a stop, including a provider or adapter error that re-wraps or echoes the text with a new Error and loses the name. That is a misclassification of a provider error as a stop signal, and the reverse failure, a real stop whose name was lost, is only partly covered by the same fragile text match. The message fallback is a symptom of the root cause: the stop marker is not carried across provider boundaries in a typed form. The predicate also has no in-repo caller under src/, so its effect depends on external consumers.
findings.recommendedAction: Carry a typed marker that survives re-wrapping, for example a code property or a cause chain checked by identity, and drop the message-prefix fallback. If the fallback must stay for compatibility, restrict it to errors that the module itself created and document it. Add a test for a provider Error whose message starts with the prefix but whose name is not WorkflowStopRequested.

findings.title: Disk stop-intent read failures are silently swallowed in the poll
findings.evidence: The poll in createWorkflowStopSignal calls readWorkflowStopIntent(...).catch(() => undefined), so any read error is treated as 'no stop intent'. The synchronous path throwIfWorkflowStopRequested does not catch and lets the read error propagate.
findings.rationale: The two stop-detection paths handle the same read differently. In the poll, a persistent read failure, such as a permissions or I/O error on the intent file, means a durably written stop is never honored from the disk path. The launch-signal path is the only remaining fence. A transient failure only delays the stop until the next 200ms poll. The persistent case is the reliability risk. Severity and confidence are moderate because this depends on the failure mode of readWorkflowStopIntent, which is not in the evidence set.
findings.recommendedAction: Fail closed or surface the error: on a read error, record it and retry, or abort with a stop-pending error, rather than mapping it to undefined. Make the poll and the synchronous check handle read errors the same way. Confirm the behavior of readWorkflowStopIntent for a missing file versus an unreadable file.

findings.title: Public summary field launchRetryAttempts renamed to launchRetries, breaking the documented contract
findings.evidence: SPEC.md T3 declares both outputRetryAttempts and launchRetryAttempts as public contract names read by external tools. The code exports outputRetryAttempts (line 32) but exports launchRetries (line 33) and computes it at line 107. No occurrence of launchRetryAttempts exists anywhere in the repository outside SPEC.md. HEAD commit message 654f639 reads 'shorter retry field name', which indicates the rename was intentional in this commit. The git diff could not be inspected with the enabled tools, so the exact prior field name in HEAD is inferred from the spec and commit message.
evidenceQuotes: - **T3.** 요약의 `outputRetryAttempts`와 `launchRetryAttempts`는 모든 작업의 재시도 횟수 합이며,
reviewerEvidenceQuotes: - **T3.** 요약의 `outputRetryAttempts`와 `launchRetryAttempts`는 모든 작업의 재시도 횟수 합이며,
findings.rationale: Consumers of the terminal summary that read launchRetryAttempts will get undefined after this change, with no error raised. The field is named as a public contract in the spec, and external tools depend on it, so a rename without a compatibility alias or versioned schema is a breaking change. The inconsistency also leaves the summary with mixed naming: outputRetryAttempts keeps the long suffix while launchRetries drops it. Renaming a public field is a compatibility regression even when no in-repo caller reads the old name.
findings.recommendedAction: Restore the public name launchRetryAttempts in WorkflowTerminalSummary and in the computation at line 107. If a shorter name is needed, add it as a new field and keep the old field populated for a deprecation window, then update SPEC T3 and record the change as a breaking change. Keep the two retry fields consistently named.

findings.title: Stop-poll default and floor diverge from SPEC S3
findings.evidence: createWorkflowStopSignal sets the default pollMs to 200 and clamps it with a floor of 1ms. SPEC S3 requires a 50ms default and a floor of 10ms, so a stop is detected up to 200ms late by default, and callers can request 1–9ms polling that the spec forbids. No in-repo caller passes pollMs, so the default is the effective behavior.
evidenceQuotes: 중지 감시 주기(`pollMs`)의 기본값은 50ms이고, 호출자가 더 작은 값을 주어도 10ms보다
reviewerEvidenceQuotes: 중지 감시 주기(`pollMs`)의 기본값은 50ms이고, 호출자가 더 작은 값을 주어도 10ms보다
findings.rationale: S3 is a stated contract. Code has a 200ms default and 1ms floor, which is 4x slower than the spec default and 10x below the spec floor. This affects stop latency for foreground and background runs. The commit message 'stop: poll less often' suggests the default was raised deliberately, so the spec and code now disagree on purpose or by accident. The lower floor also means a caller can request polling the spec forbids, and that breaks the contract for external callers.
findings.recommendedAction: Decide whether the spec or the code is authoritative. If the spec stands, change the default to 50 and the clamp to Math.max(10, ...). If 200ms is intended, update SPEC S3 and record the change. Either way, add a unit test for the default and the floor, since S3 has a test requirement under Q1.

findings.title: SPEC Q1 requires unit tests for all 12 S/C/T items, but none exist
findings.evidence: SPEC.md Q1 (line 40) requires a unit test for every S/C/T item (S1-S7, C1-C2, T1-T3, 12 items). The repo has no test files (glob and content searches for test/spec files and test-framework references found none outside .agent-workflow/ and .git/). package.json defines only a typecheck script and no test runner dependency. tsconfig.json includes only src/**/*.ts. The stop, cancellation, and terminal behaviors are therefore not verified by any executable test.
evidenceQuotes: - **Q1.** 위 S·C·T 항목마다 그 동작을 확인하는 단위 테스트가 있어야 한다.
reviewerEvidenceQuotes: - **Q1.** 위 S·C·T 항목마다 그 동작을 확인하는 단위 테스트가 있어야 한다.
findings.rationale: This is an unmet requirement in the spec, and it leaves the S/C/T behaviors unguarded. Relevant examples are the S3 pollMs floor, the S4 read-error asymmetry between the watch path and throwIfWorkflowStopRequested, the S5 dispose rule, the C2 recursion guard, and the T3 public field names. Regressions in these areas would pass the current typecheck. This is reported once as the root gap, with the missing test runner and absent tests as its symptoms.
findings.recommendedAction: Add a test runner (for example node:test or vitest) and a "test" script to package.json. Then add at least one unit test per S1-S7, C1-C2, and T1-T3 item, using the SPEC wording as the assertion. Include the S4 read-error asymmetry, the S3 10ms floor, and the T3 field names. Extend tsconfig.json or the test config so the tests are type-checked.
